newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Explorers Index gains 0.12 pct in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian Explorers Index gains 0.12 pct in week.

text.p: Perth stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd said its Australian Explorers Index struggled in the week to Friday, falling 107.7 points or 3.31 percent. The All Ordinaries Index rose 0.69 percent.
May 2 Apr 25 pct 1 Month pct 1 Year pct
NOTE: The explorers index (base 500, March 1992) tracks the performance of 88 small capitalisation exploration companies.
Eyres Reed analyst Glen Colgan said the fall came despite a flood of quarterly exploration reports, with falls outstripping gains by seven to two.

Best performances in the week included thinly traded Kurnalpi Gold emerging gold producer Gindalbie Gold, copper hopeful Majestic Resources, and Titan Resources, which rose in anticipation of results from their drilling at the Goodyear nickel discovery.
Colgan said fall were recorded across the board, with recent strong performers running out of steam including Pharaoh Metals, Money Mining , Helix and Nugold Hill.
Some exciting drill results in the resource sector last week led to very heavy trading volumes in selected stocks.

"There was a roller coaster ride on Carpenter Pacific, having traded at 38 cents last Friday, they opened at 70 cents on Monday and fell back to close at 32 cents. The market is now waiting for further results from Mt Kare," Colgan said.
Volume in Carpenter CPC.AX was a massive 26 million shares.

"Capricorn Resources announced big hit at their Roundtop project - a joint venture with Forrestania. They announced the highest grade of mineralisation to date, 11.9 metres of eight percent nickel. This saw the shares jump to 38 cents on very high volume," Colgan said.
Other gains came from Centamin, Pharaoh and Egerton Gold.
